memory_candidates.content: In this repo's orchestrator handoff schema, two continuation-pointer forms coexist and are already both accepted by validate-handoff.sh: a flat top-level `continuation_path` string (documented in context/contracts/wrap-up.md, the H9 canonical schema, and the ONLY form the sole active writer -- general-implementation-hard-agent.md's H9 Stage 5 -- actually emits) and a nested `continuation_context: {handoff_path, orchestrator_mode}` object (documented in docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md, but written only by skill-base.sh's skill_write_orchestrator_handoff, which has zero callers). Any code that decides 'is a continuation available' from .orchestrator-handoff.json (orchestrate-triage-classify.sh, skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md Stage 4) must check BOTH forms or it will silently miss every hard-mode-written partial handoff.

cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md's H9 Stage 5 wrap-up template hardcodes `"continuation_context": null` with no instruction anywhere in the file for populating it on partial/blocked status (unlike core and lean's explicit population instructions for continuation_path). cslib hard-mode partial handoffs therefore never carry any continuation pointer regardless of the classifier fix chosen -- a separate, narrower defect from the writer/predicate mismatch.
